Let the number of gold coins be \(G\) and silver coins be \(S\). We know:

\(G + S = 110\)  
\(G = S + 30\)

Substitute the second equation into the first:  
\((S + 30) + S = 110\)  
\(2S + 30 = 110\)  
\(2S = 80\)  
\(S = 40\)

Then \(G = 40 + 30 = 70\).

Answer: 70
reasoning: We are given: "Gretchen has 110 coins. There are 30 more gold coins than silver coins. How many gold coins does Gretchen have?" So we need to set up an equation. Let G = number of gold coins, S = number of silver coins. We know G + S = 110, and G = S + 30. Substitute: (S + 30) + S = 110 => 2S + 30 = 110 => 2S = 80 => S = 40. Then G = 40 + 30 = 70. So Gretchen has 70 gold coins. Answer: 70.
